Quick summary from initial triage (15m):
- Evidence: correlated NVIDIA driver traces from their traces + our metrics show repeated allocations failing on a small subset of GPUs servicing HP-4721. Kernel logs contain OOM and "cudaMalloc failed" during long prefix requests.
- Observed pattern: memory footprint grows across a sequence of long prompts (KV cache blow-up for sessions with long histories). When combined with fragmented slab allocations we see allocation failures that lead to retry cascades and 503s. Not universal — appears in ~4% of their pods (same host class).

Immediate mitigations I recommend (safe, low-risk):
A) Pin Hyperion routes to rwd-xxl-qa@v1.3-quant (smaller memory footprint) for the next 60 minutes
B) Apply per-tenant max_tokens cap of 512 and set session-prefix-eviction to aggressive
C) Enable burst autoscale for their pool (add 2 GPUs from spare pool) and temporarily route low-priority traffic to CPU fallback (best-effort only)
D) Roll an emergency driver / kernel config to reduce fragmentation (requires node restart — high impact, avoid unless mitigations A–C fail)

I’ll prepare an incident note and attach our runbook. If we proceed with A–C now we expect p99 to drop within 10–20 minutes for affected requests; 503s should drop significantly.

Attaching: incident_runbook-v2.pdf (runbook excerpt + mitigation steps)

— Monica
